lessons.subject: English
lessons.title: Relative clauses
lessons.summary: Add information to a sentence with who, which, where, when, whose or that.
lessons.curriculum: Year 5 English: relative clauses beginning with who, which, where, when, whose or that
pages: A relative clause adds information about a noun. It often starts with who, which, where, when, whose or that.
For example: ‘My aunt, who lives in Leeds, is a nurse.’ The relative clause tells you more about my aunt.
Use ‘who’ for people and ‘which’ for things. For example: ‘The bike, which was red, had a flat tyre.’

check.question: Which word fits the gap in ‘The boy ___ won the race was tired’?
check.explanation: Use ‘who’ for people: the boy who won the race.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Percentages
lessons.curriculum: Year 5 maths: recognise the per cent symbol (%), understand per cent as parts per hundred, and write percentages as fractions and decimals
pages: Per cent means ‘out of 100’. The symbol for per cent is %.
50% means 50 out of 100. That is the same as one half.
You can write a percentage as a fraction or a decimal. 25% is 25 out of 100, which is 0.25.

lessons.subject: Science
lessons.title: Earth, Sun and Moon
lessons.summary: Find out how the Earth and Moon move, and why we have day and night.
lessons.curriculum: Year 5 science: describe the movement of the Earth and Moon, and use the Earth's rotation to explain day and night
pages: The Earth travels around the Sun. One trip around the Sun takes about 365 days, which is one year.
The Moon travels around the Earth. One trip takes about 4 weeks.
The Earth spins on its axis once a day. When your side of the Earth faces the Sun, it is day. When it faces away, it is night.

check.question: Why do we have day and night?
options: The Sun travels around the Earth
The Earth spins on its axis
check.explanation: The Earth spins once a day, so each place faces the Sun and then faces away.

lessons.subject: Geography
lessons.title: Latitude and longitude
lessons.summary: Use imaginary lines on maps and globes to find places.
lessons.curriculum: Key stage 2 geography: latitude, longitude, the Equator, the hemispheres and the Prime (or Greenwich) Meridian
pages: Maps and globes have imaginary lines to help us find places. Lines of latitude run east to west. Lines of longitude run north to south.
The Equator is the line of latitude around the middle of the Earth. It splits the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
The Prime Meridian is the line of longitude at 0 degrees. It runs through Greenwich in London.

check.question: What is the line of latitude around the middle of the Earth called?
check.explanation: The Equator runs around the middle of the Earth.
